## Why look into <u>polypharmacy in women</u>? {data-section="lvl2"}

- Historically women have been underrepresented in clinical studies. 
- Only mandatory to have women in studies in mid-90'ies

\

![](illustrations/screenshots/table_women_underrep.png){width="100%" fig-align="right"}

:::{.small-text-link}
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9043984/
:::

## Why look into polypharmacy in women?  {data-section="lvl2"}

:::{.incremental}
1. Polypharmacy becoming more common
2. Women are underrepresented in clinical studies.  
:::

## How do we model effects? {data-section="lvl2"}

1. Overrepresentation of Diagnosis, medication and tests w. frequentist statistics. 
2. Bayesian estimation when possible - i.e. when we have informative priors. 
3. Hopefully I can fit in some neural networks.

## Contraceptives hi-jack the natural cycle: {data-section="lvl3"}

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="30%"}
3 kinds (for now): 
:::

:::{.column width="70%"}

\ 

1. Pills: Progesterone and Estrogen
   - Regular bleeding, medium risk 
2. Pills: Progesterone 
   - Irregular bleeding, low-risk
3. IUD: Progesterone
   - Irregular bleeding, low risk  
:::

## Pipeline: {data-section="lvl3"}

1. Define usage periods
2. Apply exclusion criteria 
3. Find some outcome you want to measure 
4. Poisson-regression
